purpose: GliomaAI is a 3D Slicer extension for researchers and clinicians studying brain tumors that preprocesses preoperative T1-CE and FLAIR MRI volumes and classifies gliomas into low-grade (LGG) or high-grade (HGG) using pretrained 3D CNNs with Grad-CAM explainability overlays.
summary: GliomaAI provides MRI preprocessing (resampling, RAS reorientation, SynthStrip skull stripping, N4 bias correction, z-score normalization), 3D CNN LGG/HGG glioma grading, and 2D/3D Grad-CAM visualization. It meets all three Slicer Extensions Index admission requirements: it is safe (local inference, SHA-256 checksum verification for downloaded models), clearly licensed under MIT (including third-party notices for SynthStrip), and has a valid catalog entry and CMake configuration. Several non-blocking bugs should be fixed by the author, notably an uninitialized `suffix` variable in `process()` when RAS reorientation is unchecked, shared `SlicerParameterName` bindings across all three input volume selectors in `GliomaClassifier.ui`, and a user confirmation prompt before installing TensorFlow. 🟢 Recommend merge

safety.rationale: Inspected all Python files, CMake files, and documentation. Processing runs locally, temporary files use `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`, and downloaded TorchScript models from the project's GitHub releases are verified with hardcoded SHA-256 checksums via `slicer.util.downloadFile`. No data exfiltration, command injection, or prompt manipulation was found.

environment.rationale: PyTorch is properly initialized via `PyTorchUtils` and declared in `build_dependencies` and `EXTENSION_DEPENDS`. No packages are installed at startup or import time, though `tensorflow==2.19.1` and `nipreps-synthstrip` are installed via `pip_install` on first use of those features without a confirmation dialog.

packaging.rationale: Inspected `CMakeLists.txt` and `GliomaClassifier/CMakeLists.txt`. All Python scripts under `PreProcessing/`, UI files, icons, and `Resources/Models` are properly installed, and `EXTENSION_DEPENDS` matches `build_dependencies` (`PyTorch`). Two pretrained models (15 MB and 30 MB) are committed to the repository.

license.rationale: Inspected `LICENSE.txt` (MIT License for GliomaAI code and project-trained models), `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, and `licenses/SynthStrip-MIT.txt` (MIT License for bundled SynthStrip weights). Clear permission to distribute is provided.

soundness.rationale: Inspected `GliomaClassifier.py`, `GliomaClassifier.ui`, and all `PreProcessing/*.py` modules. Found a couple of functional bugs: `suffix` in `process()` is uninitialized when `applyRAS` is unchecked (`UnboundLocalError`), all three `qMRMLNodeComboBox` widgets share `SlicerParameterName="inputVolume"` in the `.ui` file causing them to overwrite each other, and the self-test still uses template threshold code.

utility.rationale: Inspected `README.md` and module code. The extension is well-documented with clear usage instructions, prominent clinical-use disclaimers, model provenance and peer-reviewed publication references, preprocessing steps, and 2D/3D Grad-CAM visualization.

findings.title: Large TensorFlow package installed via pip without user confirmation
findings.explanation: When the user runs classification with the default H5 model (`proposed_model_final.h5`), `ensure_tensorflow_installed()` immediately calls `slicer.util.pip_install("tensorflow==2.19.1")` without asking the user for confirmation. TensorFlow is a very large download (hundreds of megabytes) that also pulls in or updates shared Python packages in Slicer's environment (such as `numpy`, `h5py`, `protobuf`, etc.), which can block the GUI thread for a long time and potentially alter packages bundled by Slicer.
findings.suggestion: Prompt the user with `slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay` before installing `tensorflow==2.19.1` (and `nipreps-synthstrip` in `apply_skull.py`), or consider converting `proposed_model_final.h5` to PyTorch/TorchScript or ONNX so the extension only needs the declared `PyTorch` dependency.

findings.title: UnboundLocalError for `suffix` in `process()` when `applyRAS` is False
findings.explanation: In `GliomaClassifierLogic.process()`, `suffix` is only initialized if `applyRAS` is `True`. If the user runs preprocessing with `applyRAS` unchecked (whether or not other options are checked), `suffix += ...` or `inputVolume.GetName() + suffix` raises `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'suffix' where it is not associated with a value`.

findings.title: UnboundLocalError when '3D Render' is checked without 'Generate XAI'
findings.explanation: In `onApplyButton_1()`, `heatmap_kji` and `xaiNode` are only defined inside the `if hasattr(self.ui, "provideXAIcheckBox") and self.ui.provideXAIcheckBox.checked:` block. If the user checks `renderXAIin3DcheckBox` ("3D Render") without checking `provideXAIcheckBox` ("Generate XAI"), evaluating `if heatmap_kji is None` raises `UnboundLocalError` instead of the intended `RuntimeError` (or automatically enabling XAI generation as stated in README line 101).
findings.suggestion: Initialize `heatmap_kji = None` and `xaiNode = None` before line 730, or automatically check/run XAI generation when `renderXAIin3DcheckBox` is checked.

findings.title: All three volume selectors in UI are bound to the same `inputVolume` parameter node property
findings.explanation: In `GliomaClassifier.ui`, `inputSelector` (line 78), `inputSelector_1` (line 308), and `inputSelector_2` (line 349) all have the dynamic property `SlicerParameterName` set to `inputVolume`. Because `self._parameterNode.connectGui(self.ui)` binds all three combo boxes to the same `inputVolume` parameter on `GliomaClassifierParameterNode`, selecting a FLAIR volume in `inputSelector_2` overwrites `inputSelector_1` (T1-CE) and `inputSelector` with the same node.
findings.suggestion: Remove `SlicerParameterName` from `inputSelector_1` and `inputSelector_2`, or add distinct `t1cVolume` and `flairVolume` fields to `GliomaClassifierParameterNode`.

findings.title: Self-test uses leftover template signature and assertions
findings.evidence:
# Test algorithm with non-inverted threshold
        logic.process(inputVolume, outputVolume, threshold, True)
        outputScalarRange = outputVolume.GetImageData().GetScalarRange()
        self.assertEqual(outputScalarRange[0], inputScalarRange[0])
        self.assertEqual(outputScalarRange[1], threshold)
findings.explanation: `GliomaClassifierTest.test_GliomaClassifier1` still contains the boilerplate threshold test from the Slicer module template. It calls `logic.process(inputVolume, outputVolume, threshold, True)` where the boolean parameters `applyRAS`, `applySkullStrip`, and `applyN4` receive `outputVolume`, `100`, and `True`, and then asserts that `outputVolume` (which `process()` does not write to) was thresholded to `100`. This test will fail when run.
findings.suggestion: Update `test_GliomaClassifier1` to call `logic.process()` with boolean flags and check the returned volume node.

findings.title: Module category is set to 'Examples' instead of 'Neuroimaging' or 'Informatics'
findings.evidence:
self.parent.title = _("GliomaAI")  # TODO: make this more human readable by adding spaces
        # TODO: set categories (folders where the module shows up in the module selector)
        self.parent.categories = [translate("qSlicerAbstractCoreModule", "Examples")]
findings.explanation: The module sets `self.parent.categories` to `"Examples"`, whereas `CMakeLists.txt` and the catalog entry use `"Neuroimaging"` and `README.md` instructs users to open `Informatics > GliomaAI`. Users following the README or looking under Neuroimaging will not find the module there.
findings.suggestion: Set `self.parent.categories = [translate("qSlicerAbstractCoreModule", "Neuroimaging")]` (or `"Informatics"`) to match the documentation and catalog entry.

findings.title: Downloaded models are written to the module installation directory
findings.explanation: Optional models downloaded at runtime by `model_manager.ensure_model()` are saved directly into `moduleDir/Resources/Models`. When Slicer is installed in a system or read-only directory (e.g. `/opt` or `C:\Program Files`), writing into the installed module folder can fail with `PermissionError`, and any downloaded models will be wiped when the extension is updated.
findings.suggestion: Store downloaded models in a user-writable cache directory (for example under `slicer.app.cachePath`) rather than the installed module's `Resources/Models` directory.

not_checked: Binary contents of bundled models GliomaClassifier/Resources/Models/proposed_model_final.h5 (15 MB) and GliomaClassifier/Resources/Models/synthstrip.1.pt (30 MB)
